Editing my review to add an observation about the neutering process: Nowadays, the animal needs to undergo a consultation and examination, and after the results are in, it's necessary to return to the clinic to receive instructions and the veterinarian's opinion before scheduling the neutering. If you're unlucky enough to find a long line, or arrive during a shift change, or even outside of business hours, be prepared to wait for hours in line just to pick up the exam results and await the veterinarian's approval, a process that could be done via WhatsApp text or phone call. Unfortunately, I had this bad luck and waited in line for 4 hours to be seen.
Grade 10

I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT AT ALL!

My dog, Scott, was 16 years old and had always been part of my family since he was a puppy. On August 21st, because he was already quite weak, I had to admit him to CVP Tijuca. It was one of the hardest decisions I've ever made, and I entrusted what I hold most precious to your team.
During his hospitalization, blood was drawn from his front paw. When I went to visit him, I found my dog ​​with that same paw injured and twisted, unable to put weight on it. He went in weak and came out worse, with an injury that didn't exist when he arrived.
Faced with the agony of seeing him in that state, I asked them to take him out of the hospital before the discharge date. They wanted him to stay, but I signed a form to remove him. They gave me no explanation about the paw — when I asked, no one told me anything, and the feeling was that he was injured when they put the needle in.

At home, the situation worsened: he could barely stand and began having focal seizures. I had to rush him to another clinic, where the doctor told me there was nothing more they could do.
I want to make it clear: I am not accusing CVP Tijuca of my Toto's death. He was 16 years old and arrived already debilitated — I acknowledge that. My complaint is not about the clinical outcome, but about the lack of care during hospitalization: my dog ​​left there injured, without improvement, and without any accountability from the clinic, which only charged me.
To top it all off, even the delivery of the exams was a hassle: they told me to get them from the app, but there was nothing there. They even wanted me to pick them up in person. Only after I refused did they send the exams, saying it was an "exception."

I wouldn't recommend this clinic to my worst enemy. The only thing that matters to them is money. I took my dog ​​there on July 8th for a consultation because his eyes were irritated. The next day, I took him for an ultrasound and blood tests. On July 11th, I went to pick up the results and found out that his glucose level was 298 and he had liver problems, with a recommendation to see an endocrinologist urgently. I contacted them to schedule an appointment, and they scheduled it for July 23rd. I explained that it was urgent, went to the clinic, and begged the receptionist to schedule it for an earlier date, but I was ignored. On July 21st, he stopped eating, was bleeding from his nose and eyes, and they hospitalized my dog. From then on, it was just wasted money. In the end, we paid almost 4,000 reais in total for nothing. My dog ​​died on July 26th, and even then, only an hour before passing away. They tried to force me to pay for a blood transfusion and a 400 reais test to see if he had tick-borne disease, even though I told them he never had ticks. Now I'm here, without the love of my life, because they took 15 days to start the diabetes treatment, which they knew he had since July 11th, not to mention the times I had to bring food and medicine even though I was paying 290 reais per day for hospitalization. I will never set foot in that cursed place again in my life.

In March 2026, my mother's dog suffered a ruptured testicle. I rushed him to the veterinary clinic, where, after examination by the veterinarians, emergency surgery was recommended, something I had already expected. Along with the surgery, I also had to pay for the post-operative hospitalization, which I also expected and was willing to do regardless of the cost. During this hospitalization, they requested two units of blood, but my wife is a veterinarian and, looking at his parameters, saw that there was no need for two units immediately, as the bone marrow was responding well; one was already enough to improve the animal's anemia. We sent a blood bag, and the hospital started insisting on another bag. Monitoring the animal's daily parameters, we saw that although his bone marrow was responding well, his hematocrit levels continued to decline, and an infection was worsening. That's when my wife intervened and asked them to take some action regarding the infection, because they were so insistent on the blood bag, but the blood bag wouldn't help if they didn't resolve the progression of the infection. That's when they changed the antibiotic to a stronger one, and my dog ​​started to respond and recover (we did another blood bag because they let it get to a point where the dog became anemic again). Finally, we were discharged, and we continue medicating the dog at home.

On April 24, 2026, approximately a month later, my mother called me and said that the dog was weak. My wife and I went to her house, and the animal was lifeless, with a white mouth. My wife, based on her experience, told me that she would recommend euthanasia, since we were talking about a 16-year-old golden retriever who could no longer walk properly and was not able to have a good quality of life. Furthermore, my mother could no longer afford treatment, considering that we had already spent more than 10,000 reais on the first attempt, and that no matter what we did, the dog could no longer withstand another transfusion.

I took the dog back to the veterinary clinic and they treated us as an emergency. We arrived with the dog unconscious at the clinic. We redid his blood tests; the infection had returned with more force and the dog's anemia was at 4%. The veterinarian who treated us herself said that the animal's parameters were not consistent with life, that she had never seen anything like it before. She agreed with my wife that their chances were very low and that he probably wouldn't survive the transfusion, but even so, she wasn't going to recommend euthanasia because there was still a chance. In other words, they wanted to squeeze as much money as they could out of the animal before it died. I told them I didn't have any more money to help my mother and that she couldn't afford it. Just the hospitalization for the transfusion, plus the blood bags, would cost over 3,000 reais, and as she herself said, even then the chances of him surviving were very low, considering the dog's age, the fact that he couldn't walk properly anymore, and everything he was going through. We preferred euthanasia to end his suffering. The veterinarian not only refused, but left the room, leaving me and the dog dying there for hours. When I decided to look for someone to find out where the doctor was, they told me I was free to go. In other words, I spent more than 3 hours in a consultation room for nothing with my dog ​​suffering. I had to leave with him under a hot sun to find another clinic where the veterinarians were much more humane and immediately understood that there was no longer any logic in prolonging all that suffering.

In addition to all of this, the clinic does not issue invoices for services; they only issued one when I demanded it, as it was my right, and even then, the invoice did not itemize the services.

And another complaint I would like to make, in addition to everything I have reported, is that on the day they collected my dog's blood for the last time, they also used expired product in the process. The case will be reported to the consumer protection agency (PROCON) in Rio de Janeiro.

Terrible experience with emergency care by Dr. Vitória and bureaucracy in the post-hospitalization visitation, which took away my possibility of a final goodbye to my beloved friend of more than a decade.
The only reason the rating wasn't 0 was because of the extremely dedicated and humane care from Dr. Amanda, she is truly to be commended. She was responsible for the night shift the only night my beloved dog was hospitalized before he passed away. And this dedication, giving me news about him in the middle of the night, immediately, was my consolation. My boy wasn't alone. Someone was really looking after him, and that someone was Dr. Amanda.
The doctors responsible for the abdominal ultrasound exam also deserve praise. Very serious, dedicated, and committed to getting as close as possible to a diagnosis so that he could be treated as soon as possible.
As for the clinician's care, it was regrettable. Not due to a lack of technical skill, although she prescribed a high-calorie diet for a patient suspected of having pancreatitis, even after I asked if that was indeed the case (the endocrinologist herself confirmed that she had done well to buy low-fat convalescent food), but perhaps she doesn't take her work seriously in terms of ethics and humanity and expects a pet owner to simply accept the treatment recommendation without question. Being well-informed about every detail of my animal's condition, the exact severity, and the medical opinion on treatment in the hospital or at home are fundamental so that I, in place of my dog, who cannot speak, can make a decision with the proper INFORMED CONSENT. I take the veterinary profession seriously. Being face-to-face with a dog that suddenly became debilitated overnight, without a definitive diagnosis, only suppositions, and seeing this doctor, who should have clarified my doubts so I could make a decision, IMPATIENT AND VISIBLY ANNOYED BECAUSE I WAS ASKING QUESTIONS AND WANTING A DETAILED EXPLANATION, simply because I wasn't in the medical field "since I wouldn't understand the vocabulary," was absurd. I only suppressed the response due to the urgency of giving my little dog attention. But I will never forget her response to my companion, who only asked about hospitalization or home treatment: "I said, it would be the internet action, but SHE DOESN'T WANT TO UNDERSTAND..." SHE, AS IF I WERE JUST ANYONE. Madam Doctor, what lay pet owners, who know how to speak and understand the Portuguese language, want is not to question the doctor, but to understand the situation exactly in order to make a decision that they will carry with them for life, BASED ON INFORMATION RECEIVED AND DOUBTS CLEARED. A regrettable attitude. I am sure that my point of view is based on a resolution from the CFMV (Federal Council of Veterinary Medicine). Review your service approach.
Regarding the excessive bureaucracy in the visitation: There was no one, NO ONE, BESIDES ME to visit an animal. I arrived an hour before the initial time, out of concern. I waited 1 hour in the empty reception area while my animal was alive, only to wait until 9 am when they received my animal, which had died a few minutes earlier. I was later told by the doctor who attended me that if she had known I was there, she would have called me earlier. But there is no direct communication between the reception and the inpatient unit so that they could be notified of my arrival.
The receptionists were wonderful. But if there is no protocol in place instructing them to notify the owner of their arrival, it is difficult to demand this from them. This failure on the part of the service provider is regrettable.
And lastly, it is worth remembering that a clinic is a service provider. I am not obligated to trust Instagram photos showing the inpatient ward, which may not be accurate, nor anyone's word. I was not allowed to see the facility from the outside, through the door, so I could judge whether it was comfortable for my animal or not. This would not have disturbed the other patients or the routine. The lack of transparency and publicity regarding the inpatient ward leaves a feeling of doubt about its quality, which was very unpleasant and creates insecurity for other future situations.

Yesterday, Dr. Nathália performed surgery on my dog's mouth, and everything went well! I was quite apprehensive about the anesthesia, but everything went smoothly. I only missed two things… I thought the post-surgery contact was very slow; I left her at 11:20 am and only heard back that she was okay at 2:30 pm, which caused me a lot of anxiety. And also, not having contact with the doctor after the surgery. I think it would be interesting for her to show the teeth that were extracted as a way to raise awareness among owners about the necessary care routine from now on. I thought she would talk to me, but I didn't even see her at the clinic. I understand that she has very restricted hours, but this contact is super important. I received information from the vet that her mouth was in critical condition, but I wasn't given any guidance on how to prevent this, since brushing a dog's teeth is always a struggle. But, even so, I am grateful for the treatment that was provided. It's very difficult for French Bulldog owners to perform any procedure because of the anesthesia; it was my dog's first time in 10 years and everything went well!

I wanted to thank the Tijuca unit. I was very apprehensive about neutering my 6-year-old Shih Tzu. After a lot of research, I found the Tijuca Clinic and checked the reviews. The price is unbelievable. The place is beautiful, clean, and all the staff are super polite. I want to thank the anesthesiologist and Dr. Rodrigo, who were incredibly caring and attentive during and after the surgery. My pet went in at 10:30 am and left at 3:30 pm. He was already doing great, a little fussy but perfectly fine. The recovery was excellent. The stitches are barely noticeable. Tomorrow will be 15 days, and I'll take him to the appointment to see if any stitches need to be removed, but my pet is already back to his normal routine. I'm incredibly grateful to the whole team!

I sought to schedule an ophthalmology appointment for my dog ​​who needs an evaluation. I confirmed the day and time proposed by reception and everything was fine.
Since Carnival came around, I thought it best to send a message confirming the appointment on Monday (23). However, even after confirming with the receptionist via WhatsApp, they didn't schedule my appointment.

I was informed that they hadn't scheduled it and that the only option was to reschedule the appointment for another week.

When it's a general practitioner, that's fine, but with a specialist, it's because the dog/cat has something serious and needs a check-up. It's not trivial, you know.

I found it disrespectful to the customer, the receptionists lacked preparation, and the system apparently doesn't work for scheduling.

Even after sending a screenshot of the previous conversation, they said nothing could be done.

I didn't even get the chance to have the appointment, so I thought it was terrible, and I believe that anyone looking for a specialist should seek more serious places to treat their pet.
